Highlight 1 · Progress

Track progress where the work is

Always visible: implemented count and percentage, plus ❓ open questions, ⚠ needs review, ○ not started.
Roll-ups per node: 3/3, 6/12, 132/153.
Status per Map Instruction: Not started · Implemented · Question.
  • Focus on what is left. Filter the tree by status, “Mapped only” or “Changed only”.
  • Doubts stay with the instruction. Mark it as Question and add a note, so it is not lost among finished work.
  • Fast bulk updates. “Mark all implemented” for a node, or for every not-started instruction below it.
  • Status is derived, not typed. A node's state comes from its instructions, so numbers never drift apart.
GEFEG Guideline Viewer · prototype4 / 8
  • The unit of tracking is the Map Instruction, because that is the unit of work for a developer.
  • The bar at the top is the answer to “how far are you?”. I can give that answer in two seconds.
  • When something is unclear, I flag that very instruction as Question. It shows up in the counters and in the tree.

Highlight 2 · Questions

Ask in context, not in a chat thread

One thread per question, attached to the field. The BA's reply sits right below it.
Type @ and pick the field. The BA gets a clickable reference.
Ctrl+V pastes a screenshot into the question.

Attached to the spot

On a field, or on one specific instruction.

Clear status

Waiting for BA BA replied Closed

Easy to find

“Questions (11) · 3 waiting”, filter by status, “Go to field”.

Stays on topic

Follow-ups go into the same thread, not a new message.

GEFEG Guideline Viewer · prototype5 / 8
  • The question lives on the field it is about. Nobody has to ask “which one do you mean?”.
  • The @ reference is the shortcut for the BA: one click and they are on the node. It can point to other fields too, as in this thread.
  • Screenshots can be pasted straight in, for the cases where a picture says more than the text.
  • The status tells both sides whose turn it is: waiting for BA, BA replied, closed.

Highlight 3 · Working with the BA

Works without a server, and gets better with one

Today no server to host it

An offline round trip. The BA needs no login and no installation.

Exportquestions → HTML
›
BA repliesin the page, saves
›
Importreplies, merged by id
The BA's page: only fields with questions, “Next unanswered”, paste screenshots.

Hosted on a server target

The same screens, shared. Developer and BA work in place.

Developerasks, tracks progress
⇄
Guideline + progress + question threadsone shared source of truth
⇄
BAreplies in place
  • Instant: questions, replies and status changes appear for both sides.
  • No files: no export, no import, no outdated copies.
  • Nothing to redesign: threads, @-references, screenshots and ids already work.
The interaction model is proven. Only the transport changes.
GEFEG Guideline Viewer · prototype6 / 8
  • Be upfront: the export and import exist because we have no server to host this on today.
  • It still works well: the BA opens one HTML file, answers, saves it, and I import the replies. Replies are merged by message id, so importing twice adds nothing twice.
  • On a server, all of that disappears. Both sides see the same page and the conversation is live.
  • The important point: the interaction model and the data are already there. Only how they travel changes.

Highlight 4 · Everyday robustness

Stays in flow, survives change

Never lose what you were writing

1 · WriteA question with @ and a screenshot
2 · Look awayAnother node, the Changes tab, the spec
3 · Come backEverything is still there
The tree keeps an @ ✎ marker on the field, and the tab shows ✎ Draft.
Drafts are kept per field in the browser: text, @-references and screenshots. Nothing is sent until you press Add question.

When the spec changes

Changes tab lists what changed and whether it is already implemented.
Inherit progress from an older version of the same guideline.
Same instruction, same content → carried over as is.
Renumbered instruction → matched by its content.
⚠ Content changed → kept, but flagged Needs review.
  • Red dots in the tree mark changed fields; “Changed only” isolates them.
GEFEG Guideline Viewer · prototype7 / 8
  • Left: while writing a question I often need to look something up in the spec. In many tools the half-written text is gone when you come back. Here, drafts are kept per field, including the @ references and screenshots.
  • Right: guidelines get new versions. Instead of starting from zero, I inherit the progress. Where an instruction's content really changed, it is not silently marked done: it is flagged Needs review.

Why it matters

A proven model for AutoSpec's BA ↔ Dev interaction

Proven in this prototypeWhat AutoSpec needs
Status per instruction, roll-up and progress bar→Implementation tracking for generated mapping specs
Questions on a field, with Waiting / Replied / Closed→Structured BA ↔ Dev conversation attached to the spec
@-references and pasted screenshots→Precise pointers, no long explanations
Inherit progress and Needs review→Regenerate a spec without losing development progress
Offline export / import→Live, in-place collaboration once hosted

Proposed next steps

  1. Review the interaction model with the AutoSpec team.
  2. Agree what to reuse: instruction keys, question threads, progress snapshots.
  3. Pilot it hosted, on one real guideline, with a BA and a developer.
Built for one developer's need. Useful for every BA ↔ developer handoff.
